chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, on the authority of Muyassir, on the authority of Abi Zayd al-Maleki that he had heard Abul Hassan (peace be upon him) say:
No one but a donkey would reject honoring and respect. The Imam was referring to good scent and a comfortable couch for resting on.

key_terms.الْوِسَادَة: cushion, pillow, or comfortable place to rest
key_terms.حِمَارٌ: donkey (metaphor for stubbornness or lack of appreciation)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by saying a donkey rejects honor in the context of scent and resting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of a donkey to illustrate the stubbornness of those who reject tangible honors like fine perfume and comfortable seating, highlighting a lack of spiritual refinement. This tradition, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the Shia emphasis on appreciating the blessings of Allah and accepting respect with grace, as refusing such simple comforts can signify a hardened heart. It serves as a practical lesson in humility and the proper reception of worldly goods as signs of divine favor.
